notes: §1985:XIV.3.2.4 GR1: DISABLE logically disconnects the MCS from the named sources or destinations; 'No action is taken when a DISABLE statement is executed which specifies a source or destination which is already disconnected, except that the value in the status key data item indicates this condition', and the program-to-MCS path is unaffected. CommunicationBinder#BindDisable binds the four forms, CommunicationEmitter#Emit calls MessageControl#Disable, and MessageControlSession#SetPath dispatches: SetPaths (INPUT, INPUT TERMINAL) and SetOne (I-O TERMINAL) return 15 and change nothing when already disabled, SetOutput judges every DESTINATION TABLE occurrence against the state at the statement's start and sets error key 5 (PB5376). Probes at 85: INPUT TERMINAL 00 then 15, unknown source 21; I-O TERMINAL 00 then 15; OUTPUT with count 0 or above the table 30 and no action; WITH KEY 00 then 15/5; WITH KEY is COBOL0902 at 2002, DISABLE COBOL0902 at 2014. The two witnesses show 00 then 15/5, a SEND to the disabled destination 10/2 held in the MCS and delivered after ENABLE (COUNT 0 then 1), and a destination named twice disconnected once (00, then 15 55). History: until the 1985 re-read 5 (2026-11-14) this row read DIVERGES, naming kb/Work PB5306 (landed), kb/Work PB5315 (landed), kb/Work PB5376 (landed); the re-read of main dc1f2dcce8 found that defect fixed by the landing of kb/Work PB5376 and records CONFORMS, upheld by an independent refuter (code read: op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-10.json, refuter op-20261114/out-reread5/rs-10-refute.json).
